card.title: MACCHI C.205
card.flavorText: The Macchi C.205 Veltro (Italian: Greyhound) was an Italian WWII fighter aircraft from the Aeronautica Macchi manufacturer and a development of the earlier Macchi C.202 Folgore. Together with the Reggiane Re. 2005 and Fiat G. 55, the Macchi C. 205 belonged to the trio of "Serie 5" Italian fighter aircraft which were centered around the Daimler-Benz DB 605 engine, which was also used in the German Messerschmitt Bf 109 fighter, and the Bf 110 and Me 210C heavy fighters. The Macchi C.205V was introduced into active service in February 1943, and soon earned recognition as one of the finest Italian aircraft during WWII. It boasted an impressive top speed at around 640 km/h (400 mph), and was armed with twin 20 mm cannons and 12.7 mm Breda machine guns. It downed numerous Allied bombers and was an equal match to the more advanced Allied fighters, such as the North American P-51D Mustang. Nonetheless, the C.205V entered service late in the conflict, resulting in only a limited production before the war’s end. A total of 262 Macchi C.205’s were manufactured, including a few variants.
